title: Find Right Interval
summary: Given an array of unique start intervals, find the index of the interval with the smallest start that is greater than or equal to the end of each interval.
statement: Given an array of unique start intervals, find the index of the interval with the smallest start that is greater than or equal to the end of each interval. If no such interval exists, return -1.
constraints: All starts are unique. Choose the smallest start >= the current end, returning that interval's original index.
A zero-length interval may choose itself. Preserve original query order and return -1 if no right interval exists.
reference_solution:
def find_right_intervals(intervals):
    from bisect import bisect_left
    order = sorted((start,index) for index,(start,end) in enumerate(intervals))
    starts = [start for start,index in order]
    result = []
    for start,end in intervals:
        position = bisect_left(starts,end)
        result.append(order[position][1] if position<len(order) else -1)
    return result

hints: Only starts matter when selecting the smallest eligible right interval.
Sort starts together with their original indices, then lower-bound each end.
Find the first sorted start >= end; return its saved input index or -1.
Lower-bound includes equality and can return the current interval when start=end. Queries remain in original order.
editorial: Sorting makes eligible starts a suffix. Binary search locates its first element, which is the minimum qualifying start. Store original indices alongside starts to undo sorting for answers. Do not force a different interval: equality and zero-length self matches are part of the contract.

tests.explanation: No start is at least 2, so the only answer is -1.
The answers are [-1,0,1]. Touching endpoints qualify, and indices refer to the unsorted input.
